author: Victoria Franco
title: Manteca daycare owner, drunk on job, admits guilt in 2025 infant death - NewsBreak
text:
By Victoria Franco ,
12 hours ago A Manteca home-based day care owner pleaded guilty this week to involuntary manslaughter and child endangerment in connection with the 2025 death of a 5-month-old boy.
On Oct. 22, 2025, Roxanne Helus was arrested in connection with the death of Christian Olvera − an infant who was in her care while she was intoxicated. The infant died from an anoxic brain injury.
Helus could face a six year sentence in state prison. She will be sentenced July 17.
Inside a Manteca courtroom Monday, June 8, Helus pleaded guilty to felony charges of child abuse/endangerment involving six children that were under her care and involuntary manslaughter.
Additionally, she pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor of driving under the influence with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.29%, more than three times the legal limit, according to the San Joaquin County District Attorney’s Office.
Another part of the plea deal was that Helus admitted an aggravating factor that she took advantage of a position of trust and confidence in committing the offenses.
Olvera's family did not respond immediately to comment regarding the plea deal taken in the case.
What happened to baby Olvera? On Oct. 22, 2025, The Manteca Police Department responded at 1:25 p.m. to Cherished Years Daycare at 2335 Merlin Lane for a report of a baby who was not breathing.
An adult was performing CPR on the child when officers arrived.
The infant was taken to a local hospital and transferred to UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital Oakland, where he died two days later.
The police department said at the time of the original call, officers determined Helus was drunk, resulting in her arrest.
Prosecutors said Helus had been caring for six children at the residential licensed daycare facility.

In an affidavit for search warrant David Poel, who is a duty sworn officer for the city of Manteca Police Department, said detectives were given permission by Helus to search for evidence related to the incident and to take photographs within the home as well as a camping trailer on the property.
Poel stated in the affidavit for search warrant that a preliminary search of the residence revealed numerous alcoholic beverages in addition to a DoorDash that was dated and time stamped earlier in the day.
Evidence showed that Helus had started consuming alcohol at about 4 a.m. and later drove two children to school while she was under the influence, prosecutors said. A test showed her blood alcohol concentration was later determined to be 0.29%.
That same morning, she ordered more than $100 worth of alcoholic beverages for delivery to the daycare.
Then, at about 11:30 a.m. she took baby Olvera to a travel trailer that was located on the same property as the daycare, prosecutors said. However, the trailer was not part of the authorized part of the licensed daycare facility and children were prohibited from being there.
Prosecutors said inside the trailer the daycare owner continued to drink while taking care of the infant.
In the process, Olvera experienced a medical emergency, but prosecutors said due to Helus’s “extreme intoxication” the child did not receive the immediate emergency medical care he required.
According to investigators, “every minute of delay in obtaining emergency assistance negatively impacted the child's chances of survival.”
The San Joaquin County District Attorney’s Office said, “The investigation further revealed that Helus' conduct created a substantial risk of death or great bodily injury to every child entrusted to her care. Her actions demonstrated a conscious disregard for the safety and welfare of the children she was legally obligated to protect.”
The affidavit for search warrant stated that Helus had talked about going to rehab in Palm Springs for alcohol abuse years prior to Olvera’s death.
Victim impact statements will be read at the sentencing hearing.
Record reporter Victoria Franco covers public safety in Stockton and San Joaquin County. She can be reached at vfranco@gannett.com . Support local news, subscribe to The Stockton Record at https://www.recordnet.com/subscribenow .
